notes: Experiment B contrast cases, authored before implementation. Proposed vs attempted vs verified; wrong-environment; negation; paraphrase; transition (v27-style) positive and negative.

questions.question: Was the deployment of revision R9 of Northstar proposed?

required_facts.fact: the team proposed deploying revision R9

questions.question: Was revision R9 of Northstar verified as deployed?

required_facts.fact: R9 was proposed and attempted but the outcome was unverified; proposing to deploy is not verifying a deployment

questions.question: Was revision R8 of Northstar verified running in production?

required_facts.fact: R8 was confirmed running in staging only, not production

questions.question: Was revision R8 of Northstar verified running in staging?

required_facts.fact: the deployment check confirmed R8 running in staging

questions.question: Was revision R7 of Northstar verified running in production?

required_facts.fact: R7 was deployed to production after the checklist passed

questions.question: Was revision R6 of Northstar confirmed?

required_facts.fact: the team did not confirm R6

questions.question: Did the Northstar team verify revision R7 in production?

required_facts.fact: same evidence as qB05 expressed in different words

questions.question: Did lazy evaluation become optional in Lazylang?

required_facts.fact: lazy evaluation is discussed but never said to become optional; optional attaches to type annotations and eager evaluation

questions.question: Did eager evaluation become optional in Lazylang?

required_facts.fact: since version 2.0 eager evaluation became optional through strictness annotations

questions.question: Are type annotations optional in Lazylang?

required_facts.fact: type annotations are optional in Lazylang
